questions.explanation: Surah An-Nur stipulates an unusually high evidentiary standard of four eyewitnesses to a Zina accusation, reflecting Islam's strong protection of individual reputation against unsubstantiated allegations.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Regarding a Hadith classified as Da'if (weak), the general position among the majority of scholars is that it
options: automatically becomes Sahih if repeated frequently enough by later scholars
must always be completely rejected and never mentioned under any circumstance
may be cited for purposes such as moral encouragement (Fada'il al-A'mal) by some scholars, but should not be relied upon to establish binding legal rulings
is equally authoritative as a Sahih Hadith for establishing law
questions.explanation: While the majority view holds that Da'if Hadiths cannot establish legal rulings, some scholars permit their cautious citation for encouraging good conduct, provided this is clearly distinguished from establishing binding law.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The term 'Tafsir' in Islamic scholarship refers to
options: the classification and collection of Hadith
the rules governing correct Qur'anic recitation
the memorisation of the entire Qur'an
the science of Qur'anic exegesis and interpretation
questions.explanation: Tafsir is the scholarly discipline devoted to explaining and interpreting the meanings of the Qur'anic text, distinct from Tajwid (recitation rules) or Hifz (memorisation).

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Hadith 'None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself' is primarily cited to illustrate
options: the principle of brotherhood and selfless goodwill among Muslims
the rules governing Zakat distribution
the conditions required for a valid Nikah
the pillars of Salah
questions.explanation: This widely cited Hadith from An-Nawawi's Forty Hadiths establishes empathy and selfless goodwill towards fellow Muslims as an essential marker of complete faith.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The concept of Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah (Oneness of Lordship) specifically refers to the belief that
options: Allah alone deserves worship
Allah alone is the Creator, Sustainer, and Controller of the universe
Allah's names and attributes are unique to Him
angels mediate between Allah and humanity
questions.explanation: Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah concerns belief in Allah's exclusive lordship over creation, sustenance, and control of the universe, distinct from Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah, which concerns the exclusivity of worship due to Him.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah (Oneness of Worship), distinct from Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah, specifically emphasises that
options: all Prophets were free from every human weakness
Allah alone is the Creator of the universe
worship in all its forms must be directed to Allah alone, without intermediaries
Allah's attributes cannot be meaningfully described
questions.explanation: Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah requires that all acts of worship be directed exclusively to Allah, a belief many pre-Islamic Arabs violated despite generally acknowledging Allah as Creator (Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah).

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Which of the following best distinguishes Shirk al-Akbar (major Shirk) from Shirk al-Asghar (minor Shirk)?
options: There is no meaningful theological distinction between the two
Minor Shirk is considered a graver sin than major Shirk
Major Shirk refers exclusively to disbelief in the Last Day

Major Shirk expels one from the fold of Islam entirely, such as worshipping idols alongside Allah, whereas minor Shirk, such as showing off in worship (Riya), does not expel one from Islam but remains gravely sinful
questions.explanation: Major Shirk involves directing worship to something besides Allah and removes one from Islam, while minor Shirk, such as ostentation in worship, is a serious sin that undermines sincerity but does not itself constitute disbelief.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Belief in Al-Qadar (divine predestination) as an article of faith is generally understood in mainstream Sunni theology to mean that
options: Allah's foreknowledge and decree encompass all events, yet humans retain genuine responsibility and choice in their actions
only the righteous possess free will
one's fate can be altered through magic or charms
human beings bear no responsibility for their actions since everything is predetermined
questions.explanation: Mainstream Sunni theology holds that Allah's all-encompassing knowledge and decree do not negate human free will and accountability, a balance central to the doctrine of Al-Qadar.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: An action classified as 'Makruh' in Islamic jurisprudence is one that is
options: obligatory, such that it becomes sinful if omitted
disliked or discouraged, whose avoidance is rewarded but whose commission is not sinful
permissible with no religious weight attached either way
strictly forbidden and sinful if committed
questions.explanation: Makruh denotes an action that is disapproved of and better avoided, earning reward for abstention, but its commission does not carry sin, distinguishing it from Haram (forbidden).

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: An action classified as 'Mubah' differs from one classified as 'Mustahabb' (recommended) mainly in that Mubah actions
options: are obligatory upon every adult Muslim
apply only to acts of worship (Ibadah)
carry no specific reward or blame either way, being simply permissible, whereas Mustahabb actions are rewarded if performed but not punished if omitted
are strictly prohibited under Sharia
questions.explanation: Mubah actions are neutral, neither rewarded nor blamed, while Mustahabb actions bring reward when performed though no sin attaches to their omission.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Which of the following correctly orders the five categories of Sharia rulings (Al-Ahkam al-Khamsah) from most strongly required to most strongly prohibited?
options: Haram, Makruh, Mubah, Mustahabb, Wajib
Mubah, Wajib, Haram, Makruh, Mustahabb
Wajib, Haram, Mubah, Makruh, Mustahabb
Wajib, Mustahabb, Mubah, Makruh, Haram
questions.explanation: The five Sharia categories run on a spectrum from Wajib (obligatory), through Mustahabb (recommended) and Mubah (neutral/permissible), to Makruh (disliked) and finally Haram (forbidden).

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Ijma, as a source of Islamic law, refers to
options: the consensus of qualified Muslim scholars (jurists) on a particular legal ruling
the personal opinion of a single scholar
the literal text of the Qur'an alone
analogical reasoning applied to new, undecided situations
questions.explanation: Ijma refers to the agreement of qualified jurists of a given era on a specific legal ruling not explicitly settled by the Qur'an or Sunnah, forming the third recognised source of Sharia.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Qiyas, as a source of Islamic law, involves
options: reaching consensus among a body of scholars
extending an existing ruling from the Qur'an or Sunnah to a new, analogous case that shares the same underlying legal reason ('illah)
receiving direct revelation from Allah
discarding all previous legal rulings entirely
questions.explanation: Qiyas is analogical reasoning, whereby jurists extend a known ruling to a new case on the basis of a shared effective cause ('illah), used when no explicit text or consensus addresses the matter directly.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Which of the following is the correct hierarchical order of the four primary sources of Sharia, from most to least authoritative?
options: Ijma, Qiyas, Qur'an, Sunnah
Qiyas, Ijma, Sunnah, Qur'an
Qur'an, Sunnah, Ijma, Qiyas
Sunnah, Qur'an, Qiyas, Ijma
questions.explanation: The Qur'an, as the direct word of Allah, ranks first, followed by the Sunnah, then the consensus of scholars (Ijma), and finally analogical reasoning (Qiyas), used where the first three are silent.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Which of the following is classified as a condition (Shart) for the validity of Salah, to be fulfilled before the prayer begins, rather than an integral pillar (Rukn) performed within the prayer itself?
options: Recitation of Al-Fatihah
Ruku' (bowing)
Sujud (prostration)
Facing the Qiblah
questions.explanation: Facing the Qiblah is among the prerequisite conditions to be satisfied before Salah begins, alongside purification and covering the Awrah, distinguishing it from the internal pillars performed during the prayer, such as Ruku, Sujud, and recitation.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Salatul Jumu'ah (Friday prayer) differs from the ordinary Zuhr prayer it replaces mainly in that it
options: consists of two rak'ahs preceded by a sermon (Khutbah), and is obligatory in congregation for adult Muslim men able to attend
consists of four rak'ahs recited silently, exactly as Zuhr is
has no fixed time of day and may be performed whenever convenient
is performed individually at home rather than in congregation
questions.explanation: Jumu'ah replaces Zuhr on Fridays with a shortened two-rak'ah congregational prayer preceded by a sermon, and is obligatory in congregation for adult Muslim men who are able to attend.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Salatul Jama'ah (congregational prayer), as opposed to praying individually, is generally considered by the majority of scholars to be
options: invalid if performed by a group larger than forty people
significantly more rewarding than praying alone, though an individual prayer remains valid
obligatory only for women
applicable only to the Friday prayer
questions.explanation: Hadith literature describes congregational prayer as carrying substantially greater reward than praying alone, though the majority of scholars still regard an individually performed prayer as valid.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Salatul Jenazah (funeral prayer) is distinguished from the five daily obligatory prayers in that it
options: is only considered valid if performed by a single individual alone
includes Ruku' and Sujud like the other prayers
is performed standing throughout, without Ruku' or Sujud, consisting mainly of Takbirs and supplications
must be performed exactly five times each day
questions.explanation: Unlike the daily prayers, Salatul Jenazah has no bowing or prostration; it consists of a series of Takbirs interspersed with supplications for the deceased, performed standing.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Which of the following actions is generally held by the majority of jurists to invalidate a person's fast during Ramadan?
options: applying eye drops
an unintentional mouthful of water while rinsing the mouth
forgetfully eating or drinking
deliberately eating or drinking during fasting hours
questions.explanation: A Hadith explicitly excuses forgetful eating or drinking from invalidating the fast; deliberate, conscious eating or drinking, however, breaks the fast and generally requires make-up (Qada).

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Categories of people granted exemption or concession (Rukhsah) from fasting Ramadan, who may instead make up missed days later or pay Fidyah, include
options: the sick, travellers, and pregnant or nursing women, depending on their specific circumstances
all adult Muslims, regardless of health or condition
only those who are especially wealthy
no category of person is ever exempted from fasting
questions.explanation: Islamic law provides concessions for categories such as the sick, travellers, and pregnant or nursing women, allowing them to defer fasting or, in some cases, pay Fidyah instead.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The standard Zakat rate applicable to gold, silver, and trade goods that have reached the Nisab (minimum threshold) and been held for one lunar year is generally
questions.explanation: The standard Zakat rate on monetary wealth, gold, silver, and trade goods held for a full lunar year above the Nisab threshold is 2.5%, distinct from the higher rates applied to agricultural produce.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Zakat on agricultural produce (Zakat al-Zuru') differs from Zakat on gold and silver in that its rate depends on
options: the type of crop alone, regardless of how it was irrigated
the nationality of the farmer
whether the land was irrigated naturally (e.g., by rainfall) or through artificial means, generally 10% versus 5% respectively
the age of the farmer cultivating the land
questions.explanation: Produce irrigated without additional labour or cost, such as by rainfall, is generally subject to a 10% Zakat rate, while produce requiring artificial irrigation is typically subject to a lower 5% rate, reflecting the additional effort and cost involved.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Zakat al-Fitr, distinct from the annual Zakat on wealth, is
options: a purely voluntary charity given only by the wealthy
calculated as 2.5% of one's annual income
paid exclusively during the Hajj season
an obligatory charity of a specified measure of food, given by or on behalf of every Muslim before the Eid al-Fitr prayer
questions.explanation: Zakat al-Fitr is a distinct, obligatory charity of food given on behalf of each member of a household before the Eid al-Fitr prayer, unlike the annual wealth-based Zakat calculated on the Nisab.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The rite of Sa'i, performed during Hajj and Umrah, commemorates
options: Hajar's search for water between the hills of Safa and Marwah for her infant son Isma'il
the Prophet's Farewell Sermon
the stoning of Iblis
Ibrahim's near-sacrifice of his son
questions.explanation: Sa'i, the ritual walking between Safa and Marwah, commemorates Hajar's desperate search for water for her son Isma'il, which tradition holds led to the miraculous spring of Zamzam.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The rite of Ramy al-Jamarat (stoning of the pillars) during Hajj symbolically commemorates
options: the Prophet's migration to Madinah
Ibrahim's rejection of Satan's temptations not to sacrifice his son
the delivery of the Farewell Sermon
the building of the Ka'bah
questions.explanation: The stoning of the pillars re-enacts Ibrahim's rejection of Satan's repeated attempts to dissuade him from obeying Allah's command regarding his son, symbolically driving away temptation.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: A pilgrim who performs Umrah first, exits Ihram, and then re-enters Ihram to perform Hajj separately within the same pilgrimage season is performing which type of Hajj?
options: Hajj Qiran
Hajj Mabrur
Hajj Tamattu'
Hajj Ifrad
questions.explanation: Hajj Tamattu' involves performing Umrah first, exiting the state of Ihram, and later re-entering Ihram to perform Hajj separately, distinguishing it from Hajj Qiran (both combined in one Ihram) and Hajj Ifrad (Hajj alone).

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Hajj Ifrad, as one of the three recognised methods of performing the pilgrimage, involves
options: performing Umrah and then exiting Ihram before beginning Hajj separately
performing Hajj without ever visiting the Ka'bah
performing Umrah and Hajj simultaneously within a single, unbroken Ihram
performing only Hajj, without combining it with Umrah in the same Ihram
questions.explanation: Hajj Ifrad involves entering Ihram with the sole intention of Hajj, without combining it with Umrah, distinguishing it from both Qiran (combined) and Tamattu' (sequential with a break in Ihram).

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Under Islamic inheritance law, a daughter's share, in the absence of a son, relative to a comparable male heir of the same degree of relation, is generally
options: half the share of a male heir of equivalent relation, reflecting the differentiated financial responsibilities assigned under Islamic law
three-quarters of the male heir's share
she receives no inheritance whatsoever
equal to the male heir's share
questions.explanation: Islamic inheritance law generally allocates a male heir twice the share of a female heir of the same degree of relation, a distinction jurists connect to the differing financial obligations, such as Mahr and maintenance, assigned to men.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: A single pronouncement of Talaq (revocable divorce), as opposed to the third and final pronouncement, allows the husband to
options: never reconcile with his wife under any circumstance
reconcile with his wife during her Iddah (waiting period) without needing a new marriage contract
marry her sister immediately without restriction
dissolve the marriage automatically with no waiting period at all
questions.explanation: A revocable (Raj'i) Talaq permits the husband to resume the marriage during the Iddah without a new contract; only after the third and final pronouncement does the divorce become irrevocable, generally requiring an intervening marriage for reconciliation.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Riba al-Fadl, one of the two main categories of prohibited interest, refers specifically to
options: profit earned from a legitimate trade partnership
interest charged on a loan repaid over time
an unequal exchange of the same type of commodity, such as unequal quantities of gold for gold, in a single transaction
charitable lending without any conditions
questions.explanation: Riba al-Fadl concerns an unequal, simultaneous exchange of a commodity for the same type of commodity, such as trading unequal weights of gold for gold, which Islamic law prohibits regardless of any delay in payment.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Riba al-Nasi'ah, the second main category of prohibited interest, refers to
options: a fixed, one-time trading fee agreed upfront
profit-sharing within a Mudarabah partnership
an unequal exchange of similar commodities in one transaction
any excess or premium charged in exchange for a delay in repaying a loan or debt
questions.explanation: Riba al-Nasi'ah is the more familiar form of interest, an increase charged specifically because of a delay in repayment, and is the type most closely associated with conventional interest-based lending.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Mudarabah, a recognised Islamic finance partnership structure, involves
options: one party providing capital and another providing labour and expertise, with profits shared according to an agreed ratio and losses generally borne by the capital provider
a fixed, guaranteed interest rate paid to the investor regardless of outcome
both parties contributing equal capital and equal labour at all times
a loan that must be repaid with an agreed premium
questions.explanation: In Mudarabah, one partner supplies capital while the other contributes skill and labour; profits are shared by agreement, but financial losses are typically borne by the capital-providing partner alone, since the working partner already loses their labour.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Musharakah differs from Mudarabah mainly in that in a Musharakah partnership
options: only one party contributes capital to the venture
all partners contribute capital (and often labour) and share both profit and loss according to agreed terms
profit is fixed regardless of the venture's actual performance
it is functionally identical to a conventional interest-bearing loan
questions.explanation: Unlike Mudarabah, where only one partner supplies capital, Musharakah involves all partners contributing capital, with both profit and loss shared according to a pre-agreed arrangement.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Islamic concept of Ihsan, described by the Prophet as 'worshipping Allah as though you see Him', represents
options: a particular category of Hadith classification
the lowest level of religious commitment in Islam
the highest level of faith, involving sincerity and spiritual excellence in worship and conduct
one of the five specific pillars of Islam
questions.explanation: Ihsan represents the pinnacle of the tripartite structure of Islam, Iman, and Ihsan described in the Hadith of Jibril, denoting sincerity and excellence of worship as though directly beholding Allah.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Amanah (trustworthiness), emphasised as a core moral value in Islam, is particularly significant because Prophet Muhammad himself was known, even before prophethood, by the title
options: As-Siddiq
Al-Ameer
Al-Farooq
Al-Amin (the trustworthy)
questions.explanation: Even before receiving revelation, Prophet Muhammad was widely respected among the Makkans for his honesty and reliability, earning him the title Al-Amin, the trustworthy one.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: As-Siddiq, the honorific title associated with Caliph Abu Bakr, reflects his reputation for
options: his immediate and unwavering acceptance of the truth of the Prophet's account of the Night Journey (Isra' wal Mi'raj)
his leadership during the Ridda wars
his military command at the Battle of Badr
his role in the final compilation of the Qur'an
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr earned the title As-Siddiq (the truthful, the one who affirms) for immediately and unquestioningly believing the Prophet's account of the miraculous Night Journey, when many others doubted.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: One significant social consequence of Uthman Dan Fodio's Jihad in Hausaland was
options: the total abolition of Islamic scholarship in the region
the establishment of a more centralised Islamic administrative system replacing the pre-existing Hausa political structures, under the Sokoto Caliphate
the introduction of an entirely new religion distinct from Islam
the expulsion of all Islamic scholars from the region
questions.explanation: Dan Fodio's Jihad restructured Hausaland's political order, replacing the existing Hausa city-state system with a more centralised, Sharia-based administration under the Sokoto Caliphate.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Nana Asma'u, the daughter of Uthman Dan Fodio, is particularly noted in the history of Islam in West Africa for her
options: position as the Caliphate's chief Zakat collector
leadership of major military campaigns
significant contributions to Islamic scholarship and women's education through poetry and teaching
central role in compiling the Qur'an
questions.explanation: Nana Asma'u was a renowned scholar and poet who made lasting contributions to Islamic education, particularly for women, within the Sokoto Caliphate.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Almoravid movement, originating among Sanhaja Berbers in the 11th century, contributed to the spread of Islam in West Africa mainly through
options: an alliance formed with European colonial powers
translating the Bible into local West African languages
peaceful trade alone, entirely without any military dimension
a combination of religious reform and military campaigns that helped extend Islamic influence into the western Sudan region, including pressure on ancient Ghana
questions.explanation: The Almoravids combined religious reform with military expansion, extending Islamic influence into the western Sudan and exerting pressure on the ancient kingdom of Ghana, contributing to Islam's deeper penetration in the region.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Ibn Battuta, the medieval traveller whose written accounts provide valuable historical evidence of Islam in West Africa, famously documented conditions in
options: the Mali Empire under Mansa Musa's successors
the Roman Empire
the Byzantine imperial court
Safavid Persia
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta's travel account, the Rihla, includes a detailed and historically valuable description of the Mali Empire he visited during the reign of Mansa Musa's successor, Mansa Sulayman.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The historical significance of Mansa Musa's pilgrimage to Makkah (1324-25 CE) lies partly in the fact that it
options: marked the very first Hajj ever performed by an African ruler in history
drew significant international attention to the wealth and Islamic character of the Mali Empire, notably through his extensive distribution of gold in Cairo
resulted in the immediate conversion of Egypt to Islam
led directly and solely to the founding of the University of Timbuktu
questions.explanation: Mansa Musa's lavish distribution of gold during his stopover in Cairo drew widespread international attention to Mali's wealth and Islamic identity, cementing the empire's reputation across the Muslim world and beyond.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Among the essential conditions for a valid Nikah (marriage contract) in Islamic law is
options: the bride's guardian belonging to a different faith from the couple
the payment of Zakat by the groom at the time of the contract
the presence of two witnesses and the free consent of both parties
a public wedding celebration lasting at least seven days
questions.explanation: A valid Nikah requires the free consent of both parties along with the presence of two witnesses to the contract, among other essential conditions such as the Mahr and a marriage guardian (Wali).

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Mahr (dower) in an Islamic marriage contract is
options: an optional courtesy with no binding legal standing
a sum shared equally between the two families
a gift owed by the bride to the groom
a mandatory payment or gift from the groom to the bride, which becomes her exclusive property
questions.explanation: The Mahr is a mandatory gift given by the groom to the bride as part of the marriage contract, becoming her exclusive personal property, which she may use, save, or dispose of as she wishes.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Iddah (waiting period) for a widow after her husband's death is generally
options: four months and ten days, or until delivery if she is pregnant
three menstrual cycles only
a fixed one year regardless of circumstance
there is no waiting period required of a widow
questions.explanation: A widow's Iddah is generally four months and ten days, extended until childbirth if she is pregnant, distinct from the shorter Iddah prescribed for a divorced, non-pregnant woman.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Iddah for a divorced woman who is not pregnant is generally reckoned as
options: a fixed period of forty days
three menstrual cycles (Quru')
four months and ten days
one full lunar year
questions.explanation: A non-pregnant divorced woman's Iddah is generally three menstrual cycles, allowing sufficient time to confirm she is not pregnant before remarriage, distinct from a widow's four-month, ten-day waiting period.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Among the specific duties attributed to individual angels in Islamic belief, the angel Israfil is primarily associated with
options: taking souls at the time of death
delivering revelation to the Prophets
blowing the trumpet (Sur) to signal the onset of the Day of Judgement
recording the deeds of human beings
questions.explanation: Israfil is traditionally identified as the angel charged with blowing the trumpet to signal the destruction of the world and, subsequently, the resurrection of humankind on the Day of Judgement.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The angel Mika'il (Michael) is traditionally associated with
options: recording the good deeds of human beings
delivering revelation to the Prophets
taking the souls of human beings at the time of death
responsibility over rain and the sustenance of creation
questions.explanation: Mika'il is traditionally associated with the distribution of rain and sustenance, distinct from Jibril, who delivers revelation, and Izra'il, who takes souls at death.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Angel of Death, often identified with Izra'il, is specifically charged with
options: taking the souls of the deceased at their appointed time
recording the sins of human beings
guarding the gates of Paradise
delivering revelation to the Prophets
questions.explanation: Izra'il, commonly known as the Angel of Death, is charged with the task of taking the souls of human beings at their divinely appointed time of death.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Among the divinely revealed scriptures recognised in Islamic belief, the Zabur (Psalms) is associated with the Prophet
options: Musa
Dawud (David)
Isa
Ibrahim
questions.explanation: The Zabur is the scripture Muslims believe was revealed to Prophet Dawud, distinct from the Tawrat given to Musa and the Injil given to Isa.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Tawrat (Torah), among the scriptures Muslims are required to believe were divinely revealed, was given to the Prophet
options: Isa
Muhammad
Musa
Dawud
questions.explanation: Muslims believe the Tawrat was revealed to Prophet Musa, one of the four scriptures, alongside the Zabur, Injil, and Qur'an, mentioned in Islamic belief as divinely revealed.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The Islamic concept of Al-Akhirah encompasses belief in several stages after death, including Barzakh, which refers to
options: the final judgement itself before Allah
the trial and testing period of a soul's earthly life
the eternal abode of the righteous in Paradise
the intermediate state or period between death and resurrection
questions.explanation: Barzakh denotes the intermediate state between a person's death and the eventual Day of Resurrection, distinct from both earthly life and the final abodes of Paradise or Hell.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: In Islamic theology, a distinction is often made between a Nabi (Prophet) and a Rasul (Messenger), whereby a Rasul is generally understood to be
options: a Prophet given a new revealed scripture or law to convey to a specific people, whereas a Nabi may continue and uphold a previous law without bringing a new scripture
always an angel rather than a human being
a title applicable only to Prophet Muhammad
identical in every respect to a Nabi, with no meaningful distinction between them
questions.explanation: While every Rasul is also a Nabi, scholars commonly distinguish a Rasul as one entrusted with a new scripture or law for a specific community, whereas a Nabi may simply reaffirm and uphold an existing revealed law.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: The concept of 'Ulul Azm' (Prophets of Firm Resolve) refers to a select group of five Prophets recognised for their extraordinary steadfastness, generally identified as
options: Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq, Ya'qub, and Yusuf
Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, and Muhammad
Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Isa, and Muhammad
Musa, Harun, Dawud, Sulaiman, and Isa
questions.explanation: The Ulul Azm Prophets, distinguished for their remarkable patience and steadfastness in the face of extraordinary trials, are generally identified as Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, and Muhammad.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: Mu'amalat, as a major branch of Islamic jurisprudence, is best distinguished from Ibadat in that Mu'amalat primarily governs
options: the recitation and memorisation of the Qur'an
acts of worship such as Salah and Sawm
human social and commercial dealings, such as contracts, trade, and marriage, as opposed to ritual acts of worship
matters relating exclusively to the Hajj
questions.explanation: Mu'amalat governs interpersonal and commercial affairs, including contracts, trade, and family matters, in contrast to Ibadat, which concerns the ritual acts of worship such as Salah, Sawm, Zakat, and Hajj.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.text: In Islamic inheritance law (Mirath), which of the following best explains why a daughter typically receives half the share of a son from the same parent's estate?
options: Daughters are excluded from inheritance entirely in most cases

The share reflects the differing financial responsibilities Islamic law assigns, since men bear the duty of maintenance (Nafaqah) for their families while women retain their share as personal wealth without such an obligation
It is a cultural custom with no basis in the Qur'an
Daughters only inherit if there is no son at all
questions.explanation: Islamic jurisprudence links the differing inheritance shares to differing financial obligations: men are responsible for maintaining their households, whereas a woman's inherited wealth remains solely hers with no equivalent duty attached.
